text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on December 23 in history.
1588 - Henry III of France ordered the assassination of Henri 3rd Duc de Guise and his brother Louis, cardinal of Lorraine at a meeting of the States General at Blois.
1732 - Richard Arkwright, British inventor and industrialist, born. Inventor of the spinning frame, he also introduced steam into his Nottingham factories.

1777 - Alexander I born. Tsar of Russia from 1801, he instituted a wide series of reforms. He took part in the destruction of French armies retreating from Russia and entered Paris in triumph to take part in peace negotiations.
1790 - Jean Francois Champollion, best known for his role in deciphering Egyptian hieroglyphics, born.
1805 - Joseph Smith, religious leader and founder of the Mormon movement, born.

1810 - Karl Richard Lepsius, German Egyptologist, born. Regarded as founder of modern archaeology, his "Egyptian Chronologies" laid the foundation for a scientific treatment of early Egyptian history. He was the first to measure the Valley of the Tombs of Kings in Egypt.
1908 - Yousuf Karsh, portrait photographer, born. From a belligerent Winston Churchill to the pouting Brigitte Bardot, he captured the famous faces of the 20th century.
1918 - Helmut Schmidt, German politician and statesman, who succeeded Willy Brandt as Chancellor in 1974 and steered the country into the major league of Western powers, born.
1933 - Marinus van der Lubbe was found guilty and sentenced to death in Germany for setting fire to the Reichstag earlier in the year.
1948 - Hideki Tojo was hanged as a war criminal; a Japanese soldier who became prime minister, he was in power when Pearl Harbour was bombed.
1950 - Pope Pius XII announced that Saint Peter's tomb had been found under the Vatican.
1953 - In the Soviet Union, Lavrenty Beria, former security police chief who played a role in Stalin's political purges, was executed for plotting to succeed him as Soviet leader.
1963 - An explosion occurred on the Greek cruise liner Lakonia and 128 passengers were killed; 908 were saved and the liner sank on December 29, some 250 miles from Gibraltar.

1972 - Andrei Tupolev, Soviet aircraft designer, died. Before World War Two, he designed bombers and the huge ANT-20 "Maxim Gorky". After the war, he designed jet airliners for the Soviet National Airline and created the world's first supersonic airliner TU-144.
1972 - In Nicaragua, a massive earthquake struck Managua which resulted in the deaths of up to 7,000 people.
1990 - People of Slovenia voted overwhelmingly in a plebiscite for the northwestern Yugoslav republic to become an independent state.
1994 - In Yugoslavia, U.N. special envoy Yasushi Akashi clinched a deal and Bosnia's Moslem-led government and rebel Serbs signed a ceasefire agreement to take effect at noon the next day.
1995 - A flash fire tore through a school prize-giving at the Rajiv Marriage Palace, in a small north Indian town, killing at least 400 people, most of them children.

1995 - In France, the charred bodies of 16 people, including three children, all members of the Order of the Solar Temple (a Swiss cult) were found on the Vercors plateau near Grenoble in what appeared to be a grisly repeat of a 1994 cult ritual in which 53 died.
